chapter: Los Angeles, Central Avenue and the Apex
title: Father's policy of showing him liquor and life first-hand
summary: His father gave him tastes of whiskey from toddlerhood so nothing would excite him later, and Royal applies that to talking honestly to kids.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And I got it all at once. Just like my dad would always give me a drink of whiskey from the time I was

a toddler. He'd give me some, if it was nothing but a half a teaspoon full, because he says, he always wanted me to know what liquor was, so that it would never excite me when it was put on me at a later age. And so, for that matter, I only managed to get drunk about twice in my life, strictly accidental. So, that was a good lesson to me, too, because he always wanted me to know exactly what was happening in life first-hand, so I wouldn't have to get it second-hand from anybody else, which is a good idea for these kids running around now that if their fathers and mothers would tell them about what marijuana is and what everything else is, not necessarily to give it to them, just tell them the truth about it, then they won't be all mixed up and upset when somebody lays it on them down the line.
